name: PARTEM
aliases: Prostatic artery embolisation versus medical treatment
question: Does prostatic artery embolisation improve symptoms more than dutasteride–tamsulosin in men with bothersome BPH symptoms despite alpha-blocker monotherapy?

design.population: 90 men aged 50–85 years with bothersome LUTS despite more than one month of alpha-blocker treatment, IPSS above 11, quality-of-life score above 3, and prostate volume at least 50 mL.
design.description: Multicentre, open-label, phase 3 superiority randomized trial
design.locator: Full text, Methods: Study design, Participants, Randomisation and masking; Results, Table 1

verdictNote: The primary nine-month IPSS difference exceeded the prespecified four-point target.
takeaway: Prostatic artery embolisation improved nine-month IPSS more than dutasteride–tamsulosin combination therapy in men with bothersome BPH symptoms despite alpha-blocker monotherapy (mean change −10.0 versus −5.7 points; adjusted difference −4.4, 95% CI −6.9 to −1.9).

reports.label: Nine-month primary and 24-month follow-up report
reports.citation: Sapoval M, Thiounn N, Descazeaud A, et al. "Prostatic artery embolisation versus medical treatment in patients with benign prostatic hyperplasia (PARTEM): a randomised, multicentre, open-label, phase 3, superiority trial." *Lancet Reg Health Eur.* 2023;31:100672. doi:10.1016/j.lanepe.2023.100672
reports.followUp: Nine-month randomized primary comparison; treatment by patient and urologist choice thereafter, with assessment at 24 months

delivery.label: Embolisation protocol
delivery.value: Femoral access under local anaesthesia; superselective bilateral prostatic-artery catheterisation, then proximal embolisation to stasis and distal embolisation with 300–500 μm Embosphere microspheres; first case at each site proctored.

values.exp: tamsulosin 0.4 mg daily through 15 days after embolisation
values.ctl: dutasteride 0.5 mg/tamsulosin 0.4 mg daily for at least nine months

delivery.label: Unilateral rather than bilateral embolisation
delivery.value: 4/45 randomized to embolisation (8.9%); two had a second attempt
delivery.locator: Full text, Results, paragraph after Table 1
delivery.note: Selective catheterisation of the second prostatic artery was not possible.
